`cd "C:/Users/dylan/Downloads/Software_Engineering/cal.diy" && gh issue view 136 --json body -q .body | grep -n -i -E "enum|IdentityProvider|OIDC\b|criterion 13|13\.|error/page|findEnabled|PublicDto" | head -20`

```text
1:Sub-issue 1 of #131. Full feature spec: `specs/oidc-sign-in/` in PR #133. Numbers in brackets, such as [39], are acceptance criteria in `specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md`.
6:#131 lets an admin add OIDC providers at run time. Today the only providers are hard-coded and configured with environment variables, and the database has no place to store a provider, its client secret, or its sign-up rules. `IdentityProvider` (`schema.prisma:367`) has no value for an OIDC user. Every other #131 sub-issue (admin backend, admin page, login flow) reads or writes this data, so it comes first.
10:Add an `OIDC` value to `IdentityProvider` and a new `OidcProvider` table with a migration. Add `PrismaOidcProviderRepository`, wired with the moduleLoader DI pattern, that is the only code that reads or writes the table. It returns DTOs, never Prisma types. The client secret is stored only as ciphertext; encrypting it is the admin service's job (sub-issue 3), not the repository's.
14:As a developer on the #131 sub-issues, I want one repository for OIDC providers, so that the admin backend and the login flow read the same data in the same way and the secret cannot leak through a query that selects too much.
18:The admin service (sub-issue 3) calls `create` with an encrypted secret. The login route (sub-issue 5) calls `findEnabled` on each auth request and gets the enabled providers in display order, without their secrets, then calls `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret` for the one provider whose flow it builds. When an admin removes a provider, the service calls `deleteWithAccounts`, and the provider and every user link to it go in one transaction.
26:1. A migration adds `OIDC` to `IdentityProvider` and creates `OidcProvider` with: `id` (cuid, primary key), `displayName` (text), `issuer` (text), `clientId` (text), `clientSecretEncrypted` (text), `scopes` (text), `allowSignup` (boolean), `allowedDomains` (text array), `enabled` (boolean), `position` (integer), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `updatedById` (nullable integer).
30:5. `findEnabled()` returns only enabled providers, ordered by `position` and then `createdAt`, as `OidcProviderPublicDto` (`id`, `displayName`, `issuer`, `clientId`, `scopes`, `allowSignup`, `allowedDomains`). It never selects `clientSecretEncrypted`. [6, 11]
34:9. `countLinkedAccounts(id)` returns the number of distinct users with an `Account` row whose `provider` is `oidc-<id>`. [36]
35:10. `deleteWithAccounts(id)` deletes the provider and every `Account` row with `provider = "oidc-<id>"` in one transaction. If either delete fails, neither happens. Deleting an unknown id throws `ErrorWithCode` not-found and deletes nothing. [37]
38:13. `yarn type-check:ci --force` passes. Code that switches over `IdentityProvider` handles `OIDC` (for example the provider name on `/auth/error`, `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/auth/error/page.tsx:39-48`, falls back to "your original login method").
39:14. Unit tests with a mocked Prisma client cover criteria 3 and 5 to 10, including a check that the `select` of `findEnabled` and `list` has no `clientSecretEncrypted` key.
45:- Mapping `oidc-<id>` to `IdentityProvider.OIDC` in `identityProviders.ts` (sub-issue 5).
60:**How a user is linked to a provider.** Use the existing `Account` table with `provider = "oidc-<id>"`, not a new column on `User`. See ADR-002 in `specs/oidc-sign-in/decisions.md`: `Account` already has `@@unique([provider, providerAccountId])` (`schema.prisma:1258`), and a column on `User` would allow only one link per user.
70:- DI pattern: `packages/features/credentials/di/CredentialRepository.module.ts`; tokens in a new `packages/features/auth/oidc/di/tokens.ts`, spread into `packages/features/di/tokens.ts`.
73:- Likely files: `schema.prisma`, the migration, `PrismaOidcProviderRepository.ts` and its test, `packages/lib/dto/OidcProviderDto.ts`, `OidcProviderRepository.module.ts`, `OidcProviderRepository.container.ts`, `tokens.ts` (two files), and `auth/error/page.tsx` if criterion 13 needs it.
```

```markdown
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Sub-issue 6 of #131. Seed and criteria numbers come from `specs/oidc-sign-in/` in PR #133 (criteria 11, 12, 21–25 in `design.md`).

#131 lets an admin add OIDC providers, but users have no way to reach them: the login and sign-up pages only render the hard-coded Google and Microsoft buttons (`apps/web/modules/auth/login-view.tsx:198-230`, `apps/web/modules/signup-view.tsx:632-734`).

Sign-in failures are also invisible today. When NextAuth cannot start or finish an OAuth flow, it redirects to `/auth/login?error=OAuthSignin` (or `OAuthCallback`, `AccessDenied`), but `login-view.tsx` never reads `error` from the URL (it only reads `callbackUrl` and `email`, `:140` and `:255`), so the user sees a normal login page with no explanation. This already affects Google and Microsoft sign-in, and it would affect every OIDC failure (provider down, [REDACTED:generic-password] client secret, expired `state`). The `/auth/error` page also has no messages for the new OIDC error codes that sub-issue 5 will emit.

### Describe the solution you'd like

1. **Provider buttons.** The login page shows one "Continue with <display name>" button per enabled OIDC provider, in the admin's order, below Google and Microsoft. Clicking it calls `signIn("oidc-<id>")`. The sign-up page shows the same buttons only for providers with "allow new accounts" on, and none when sign-up is disabled site-wide. With no enabled provider, both pages look exactly as they do today. Only each provider's `id` and display name reach the browser (the `findEnabled()` DTO from #136 also carries `issuer`, `clientId`, `scopes` and `allowedDomains`, so the server props strip it down).
2. **Login page errors.** The login page reads `?error=` and shows a clear, translated message for `OAuthSignin`, `OAuthCallback` and `AccessDenied`, with a generic fallback for anything else.
3. **Error page messages.** `/auth/error` shows messages for the new codes `missing-email`, `oidc-signup-not-allowed`, `oidc-account-exists` and `unknown-provider`, and names OIDC accounts correctly in the existing `[REDACTED:generic-password]-provider` message.

All new strings go in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`. The exact behaviour is in **User Story**, **User Scenario** and **Acceptance Criteria** below.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- **Show errors only on `/auth/error`.** We could point NextAuth's `pages.error` at `/auth/error` for every failure instead of reading `?error=` on the login page. We prefer the login page, because the user can retry or pick another sign-in method right there. The choice will be recorded in the design decisions.
- **Name the provider in failure messages ("We could not reach <name>").** NextAuth's `?error=` redirect does not say which provider failed. The options (a generic message, the "last used" value, or a parameter added by sub-issue 5) are listed under **Open Questions**.

### Additional context

- Parent: #131. Depends on #136 (sub-issue 1) for `findEnabled()`. The buttons work end to end only after sub-issue 5 registers providers as `oidc-<id>` and emits the error codes above.
- The PR can open before #136 merges: the button list comes in as a prop (empty means no buttons), and the error handling has no dependency. Wiring the props to `findEnabled()` is a final commit after #136 merges.
- Coordination: #136's criterion 13 also edits `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/auth/error/page.tsx`. Proposed: this sub-issue owns that change.
- Out of scope: see **Out of Scope** below.

### Requirement/Document

- Feature spec: `specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md` (PR #133), criteria 11, 12, 21–25.
- Customer answers on #131: 2 (site-wide disable-signup wins over the provider's switch), 3 (unverified email uses the existing `unverified-email` message), 13 (no visible change until a provider is added).
- NextAuth error codes: https://next-auth.js.org/configuration/pages#sign-in-page
```

```text
## User Story
As a user whose organization signs in through its own identity provider, I want a "Continue with <provider>" button on the login and sign-up pages, and a clear message when that sign-in fails so that I can sign in with my work account in one click, and I know what to do instead of landing on a blank login page when something goes [REDACTED:generic-password].

## User Scenario
An admin has added two OIDC providers, "Acme SSO" (allow new accounts on) and "Partner Login" (allow new accounts off), in that order. Maria opens the login page and sees the Google button, then "Continue with Acme SSO" and "Continue with Partner Login", then the "or" divider and the email form. She clicks "Continue with Acme SSO", signs in at Acme, and lands on her bookings; the next time she opens the login page, that button shows the "Last used" badge. Her colleague Sam opens the sign-up page and sees only "Continue with Acme SSO". One morning Acme's server is down: Maria clicks the button and is sent back to the login page, which now shows an error telling her the sign-in provider could not be reached and to try again later or use another sign-in method. Before this change she saw the normal login page with no message. Sam, who has no Cal.diy account, tries "Partner Login" from the login page and is sent to the error page, which tells him that provider does not allow new accounts. On an instance with no OIDC provider, the login and sign-up pages look exactly as they do today.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. **Login buttons.** The login page shows one button per enabled OIDC provider, in the admin's order (`position`), below the Google and Microsoft buttons and above the "or" divider. The label is the translated `continue_with_provider` string with the provider's display name. Clicking it records `oidc-<id>` as the last-used login method and calls `signIn("oidc-<id>", { callbackUrl })` with the page's existing `callbackUrl`. The "Last used" badge appears on that button when `oidc-<id>` was the last method used. [spec 11]
2. **OIDC-only instance.** When Google and Microsoft login are both off but at least one OIDC provider is enabled, the login page still shows the provider buttons and the "or" divider.
3. **No providers.** With no enabled OIDC provider, the login and sign-up pages render the same buttons, divider and form as before this change, and existing login/sign-up tests pass unchanged. [customer answer 13]
4. **Sign-up buttons.** The sign-up page shows the same buttons, in the same order, only for providers with "allow new accounts" on. It shows none when sign-up is disabled site-wide, by `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_SIGNUP="true"` or by the `disable-signup` feature flag. [spec 12, customer answer 2]
5. **Browser data.** The login and sign-up page props contain, for each provider, only `id` and `displayName`. A unit test fails if any other field (for example `issuer`, `clientId`, `scopes`, `allowedDomains` or a secret) reaches the props.
6. **Login page errors.** When the login page URL has `?error=`, the page shows the existing error alert with a translated message: `OAuthSignin` → the sign-in provider could not be reached, try again later or use another sign-in method; `OAuthCallback` → sign-in failed, try again; `AccessDenied` → access was denied; any other value → a generic sign-in error. The raw `error` value is never shown. Without `?error=`, no alert is shown. This also applies to Google and Microsoft sign-in. [spec 21, 22]
7. **Error page codes.** `/auth/error?error=<code>` shows its own translated message for each new code: `missing-email` (the provider did not share an email address), `oidc-signup-not-allowed` (no account exists and this provider does not allow new accounts), `oidc-account-exists` (an account with this email already exists; sign in with the original method), `unknown-provider` (this sign-in method is not available; contact your administrator). Existing codes keep their current messages. [spec 23–25]
8. **Wrong-provider name.** `/auth/error?error=[REDACTED:generic-password]-provider&provider=OIDC` names the OIDC sign-in method instead of "your original login method". Messages for `GOOGLE`, `CAL` and `SAML` are unchanged.
9. **Translations and tests.** Every new user-facing string is a key in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`; no new English text is hard-coded in components. Unit tests cover the error-code → translation-key mapping for criteria 6–8 (every listed code plus an unknown code) and the provider filtering for criteria 3–5.

## Out of Scope
- Registering OIDC providers in NextAuth, the `oidc-<id>` id, sign-in rules, and emitting the four `/auth/error` codes (sub-issue 5). This issue only displays them.
- The provider table and `findEnabled()` (#136), the admin backend and settings page (sub-issues 3 and 4).
- Linking OIDC to existing accounts (sub-issue 7), connected logins in Settings → Security (sub-issue 8), and Playwright e2e for the full OIDC flow (sub-issue 9).
- Provider logos or icons on the buttons.
- Translations for locales other than English (they fall back to English).
- Changing NextAuth's `pages.error` / `pages.signIn` configuration.
- Naming Microsoft (`AZUREAD`) in the `[REDACTED:generic-password]-provider` message, which also falls back to "your original login method" today.

## Open Questions
- Criteria 22 and 23 of the feature spec put the provider's display name in the failure message ("We could not reach <display name>"), but NextAuth's `?error=` redirect does not say which provider failed. Should the messages in criterion 6 be generic, use the last-used login value, or use a parameter that sub-issue 5 adds to the redirect?
- For `[REDACTED:generic-password]-provider` with `provider=OIDC`, should the message use a generic name (for example "single sign-on") or the provider's display name (which needs the provider id in the URL from sub-issue 5)?
- Feature spec criterion 24 (provider disabled mid-flow → "not set up correctly, contact your administrator") and criterion 25 (unknown provider id → generic sign-in error) differ. Which one does the `unknown-provider` code represent?
- #136 criterion 13 also edits `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/auth/error/page.tsx`. Does #146 own that change? (To confirm with Zach.)
- Should the sign-up page (criterion 4) ship in this PR, or in a separate PR so each stays small?

## Scope

Small. It touches the login and sign-up views and their server props, the `/auth/error` page, the `useLastUsed` login type, and translations: about 7–9 files and 200–300 lines including unit tests. It changes no schema, API or sign-in logic.
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 04:55:16Z)**_

Short answer: you can make the Google button appear with two `.env` settings. The Microsoft button can't appear at all right now unless you change code.

## Google: turn it on in `.env`

The login and sign-up pages show the Google button only when `IS_GOOGLE_LOGIN_ENABLED` is true (`apps/web/server/lib/constants.ts:1-5`, **Confirmed**). That needs both of these:

1. `GOOGLE_LOGIN_ENABLED=true`. Your `.env:140` has it set to `false`.
2. `GOOGLE_API_CREDENTIALS` set to JSON that includes `web.client_id` and `web.client_secret`. Yours is empty (I checked only that it's empty, not any values).

If you only want to see the button, placeholder values are enough:

```
GOOGLE_LOGIN_ENABLED=true
GOOGLE_API_CREDENTIALS={"web":{"client_id":"dummy","client_secret":"dummy"}}
```

Then restart the dev server and open `/auth/login` and `/signup`. With placeholder values, clicking the button just takes you to Google's "invalid client" error page. To actually sign in, you need real OAuth credentials from Google Cloud Console (see the comment at `.env.example:128-133`).

## Microsoft: currently never shown

- **Login page:** the prop is hard-coded off: `isOutlookLoginEnabled: false` (`apps/web/server/lib/auth/login/getServerSideProps.tsx:91`, **Confirmed**).
- **Sign-up page:** `signup-view.tsx:198` reads `isOutlookLoginEnabled`, but `apps/web/lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx` never passes it, so it is always `undefined` (**Confirmed**).
- **Server side:** NextAuth does register Microsoft when the `OUTLOOK_*` env vars are set (`next-auth-options.ts:337`). Only the button is hidden.

To look at it locally, temporarily change line 91 to `true`. Don't commit that.

## Seeing the error bug without any setup

Open `http://localhost:3000/auth/login?error=OAuthSignin`. Today the login page looks completely normal. That is the bug criterion 6 fixes, and it makes a good "before" screenshot for your PR's Test Evidence.

## Wording in the spec

The spec says the new buttons go "below the Google and Microsoft buttons". That's true of the code layout, but since Microsoft is never shown, in practice it usually means below Google or with no other buttons. Criterion 2 (only OIDC enabled) is the case most deployments will hit. I'd like to add a sentence to the Problem section saying the Microsoft button is currently always hidden.

I found some things in NextAuth's code that change the spec. Here they are, then the design decisions.

## Spec corrections from the NextAuth code (all **Confirmed**)

1. **`AccessDenied` goes to `/auth/error`, not the login page.** NextAuth 4.24.13 sends only `Signin`, `OAuthSignin`, `OAuthCallback`, `OAuthCreateAccount`, `Callback` and `OAuthAccountNotLinked` (among others) back to the sign-in page (`node_modules/next-auth/core/index.js:209-214`). That redirect lands on `/auth/login?callbackUrl=…&error=…` (`:167-169`). Every other code goes to `pages.error` (`:215-219`, `next-auth-options.ts:416`). `AccessDenied` is one of those (`core/routes/callback.js:85`). Today `/auth/error` shows it as "error_during_login Error code: AccessDenied". Spec AC6 needs to move `AccessDenied` to AC7.
2. **`unknown-provider` is already sent today** (`next-auth-options.ts:861`), for any provider that `getIdentityProvider` doesn't recognize. That matches feature-spec criterion 25 ("generic"), which mostly answers the spec's third open question. `new-email-conflict` (`:986`) has no message either. It's out of scope, but worth noting.
3. **When sign-up is disabled, the whole sign-up page redirects to `/auth/error`** (`apps/web/lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx:65-71`). So "no buttons when sign-up is disabled" in AC4 holds without new code. A test should still check that the redirect happens.
4. **Unit tests under `apps/**` only match `.ts`/`.js` files** (`vitest.workspace.ts:59`). A `.tsx` component test in `apps/web` would never run. This affects the testing side of every option below.

I'll update `spec.md` for points 1–3 once you've chosen.

---

## Decision 1: Where the error-code → message mapping lives

**Context.** Two pages need the same kind of mapping:
- The login page's `errorMessages` map (`login-view.tsx:131-137`) only covers credentials errors (`:161-170`).
- `/auth/error` has an if/else chain (`auth/error/page.tsx:36-56`).

This issue adds about 3 codes to the login page and about 5 to the error page.

| | **A. Shared pure module** | **B. Extend each page in place** | **C. Add codes to `ErrorCode` enum** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Change | New `apps/web/modules/auth/lib/authErrorMessages.ts`: `getLoginErrorKey(code)` and `getAuthErrorPageMessage(code, provider)`, which return i18n keys and parameters. Both pages call it. | Add entries to the `errorMessages` map in `login-view.tsx` and branches to the if/else in `page.tsx`. | Add `OAuthSignin` and the others to `packages/features/auth/lib/ErrorCode.ts`; the login page looks them up in its existing map. |
| Pros | One place to test. It's a `.ts` file, so Vitest picks it up (point 4). Good target for Stryker mutation testing (D6). | Smallest diff. Follows the code as it is now. | Reuses an existing enum. |
| Cons | One new file plus a test file. Slightly more indirection. | The logic sits inside a component and a server page. A unit test would need to render a `.tsx` file, which doesn't run in `apps/web` (point 4), so you'd fall back to manual or e2e testing. That's weak evidence for AC6–8 and gives little to mutation-test. | `ErrorCode` lists credentials and server errors (`packages/features`). Mixing NextAuth's built-in codes into it blurs what it means. It also doesn't help `/auth/error`. |
| Rules | Fits `testing-coverage-requirements.md` (team) | Conflicts with the coverage rule (team) | Changes `packages/features` for something only the web app uses (`architecture-features-modules.md`, team) |
| Size | ~+60 code lines, +80 test lines, 2 new files | ~+40 lines, 0 new files | ~+30 lines, touches a shared package |

## Decision 2: How providers reach the pages, given #136 doesn't exist yet

**Context.**
- The login and sign-up server props pass booleans today (`server/lib/auth/login/getServerSideProps.tsx:88-93`, `lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx:58`).
- #136's `findEnabled()` returns a DTO with 7 fields (#136 AC5). Only `id` and `displayName` may reach the browser (spec AC5).
- #136 has no PR. Your deadline is today.

| | **A. Props + mapper now, wire `findEnabled()` last** | **B. Stack on #136's branch** | **C. Client fetches providers** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Change | New prop `oidcProviders: OidcLoginButton[]` (`{ id, displayName }`). Add a pure function `toOidcLoginButtons(providers, { signup })` that filters by `allowSignup` and strips the other fields. Until #136 merges, the server props pass `[]`. Calling `getOidcProviderRepository().findEnabled()` is one final commit. | Branch from #136's branch, import the real DTO and the container getter, and call `findEnabled()` in the server props right away. | A public tRPC query or API route returns the button list. The views fetch it on mount. |
| Pros | You can open the PR today, with no dependency on #136. The mapper is a `.ts` unit you can test (AC3–5). | Real types end to end. No temporary type, no follow-up commit. | Server props stay unchanged. |
| Cons | The input type for the mapper is temporary (you'd copy the DTO's shape) and must match #136 later. Nothing visible changes until the final commit. | Blocked until #136 has a pushed branch. There isn't one today (context.md). The PR diff also includes #136's commits until #136 merges. | New public endpoint. The buttons appear late, so the layout shifts. Adds a tRPC dependency to the view. Costs more lines and adds API surface. |
| Rules | DTO in `packages/lib/dto/` (`data-dto-boundaries.md`, team). Call the DI container getter, not `new` (`patterns-dependency-injection.md`, team). | Same | `api-no-breaking-changes.md`: a new public API must stay stable from then on (team) |
| Size | ~+50 code lines + ~60 test lines; the final commit is ~10 lines | Same as A, without the temporary type | ~+120 lines, 3–4 more files |

## Decision 3: Naming the failed provider in messages

**Context.**
- Feature-spec criteria 22 and 23 say "We could not reach <display name>".
- NextAuth's built-in redirects carry only `error` and `callbackUrl` (`core/index.js:167-169`), so `OAuthSignin` can't carry a provider name.
- Custom codes are different: Cal's `signIn` callback builds those URLs itself (`next-auth-options.ts:1078` already adds `&provider=`), so they can carry a provider.

| | **A. Generic messages** | **B. Use the "last used" value on the login page** | **C. Sub-issue 5 adds `&provider=oidc-<id>` to custom codes** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Change | Fixed text: "the sign-in provider could not be reached…" | The login view reads `lastUsed` (`useLastUsed.tsx`, localStorage). If it is `oidc-<id>`, it looks up `displayName` in the `oidcProviders` prop and fills it into the message. | `/auth/error` reads `provider`, looks up the display name on the server, and fills it in. Built-in codes stay generic. |
| Pros | Simplest. Always correct. No dependency on other sub-issues. | Meets criteria 22 and 23 on the login page with no help from sub-issue 5. | Accurate for custom codes. It's the pattern `[REDACTED:generic-password]-provider` already uses. |
| Cons | Doesn't fully meet feature-spec criteria 22 and 23. | `lastUsed` is set before the redirect, so it can be [REDACTED:generic-password] (another tab, cleared storage). It only works on the login page (`/auth/error` is a server component). It could name the [REDACTED:generic-password] provider. | Needs agreement with sub-issue 5 and a database lookup on the error page. Doesn't help `OAuthSignin` or `OAuthCallback`. |
| Tests | Mapping unit test only | The mapper takes `lastUsed` as an input, so it's still unit-testable | Needs a mocked repository on the error page |

## Decisions I skipped (only one sensible answer)

- **`useLastUsed` type:** widen it to `` "saml" | "google" | "microsoft" | "credentials" | `oidc-${string}` `` (`useLastUsed.tsx:7`). Any alternative loses type safety.
- **Button component:** a small shared `OidcProviderButtons` component used by both views, following the Google button pattern (`login-view.tsx:198-214`). Copying the markup into both views would break `quality-simplicity.md` (team), and there's nothing else in the codebase to reuse.
- **Sign-up in this PR or a separate one:** that's a scope question, already in the spec's Open Questions, not a design question.

---

**Please choose for each decision (1A/B/C, 2A/B/C, 3A/B/C) and give your reasons in your own words.** Your reasons go into the Rationale section of `design.md`. If you'd like my recommendation, ask and I'll say how confident I am.

```text
## Design

Design decisions for #146 (sub-issue 6 of #131). Each follows the course template.

### Decision 1: Where error-code messages live

**Decision:** Map sign-in error codes to translation keys in one shared pure module, `apps/web/modules/auth/lib/authErrorMessages.ts`, used by both the login page and `/auth/error`.

**Alternatives considered:**
1. Shared pure module (chosen): `getLoginErrorKey(code)` and `getAuthErrorPageMessage(code, provider)` return i18n keys and parameters; `login-view.tsx` and `auth/error/page.tsx` call them, and a `.test.ts` file covers every code plus an unknown one.
2. Extend each page in place: add entries to the `errorMessages` map in `login-view.tsx` (`:131-137`) and new branches to the if/else chain in `auth/error/page.tsx` (`:36-56`).
3. Add NextAuth's codes (`OAuthSignin`, `OAuthCallback`, …) to the `ErrorCode` enum in `packages/features/auth/lib/ErrorCode.ts` and look them up in the login page's existing map.

**Rationale:** It keeps the mapping in one place that a unit test can reach and avoids duplicating the logic across two pages. Vitest only runs `.ts`/`.js` tests under `apps/**` (`vitest.workspace.ts:59`), so logic left inside the `.tsx` view or server page could only be checked manually; the enum option would put web-only NextAuth codes into `packages/features` and still not help `/auth/error`.

**Consequences:** Easier: unit tests for acceptance criteria 6–8, a clear target for StrykerJS mutation testing (D6), and adding future codes in one place. Harder: one new file and one more level of indirection; the pages still need a manual check that they display the returned key.

### Decision 2: How providers reach the pages before #136

**Decision:** Pass providers to the login and sign-up pages as an `oidcProviders` prop of `{ id, displayName }` built by a pure mapper, with the props set to `[]` until #136 merges and the `findEnabled()` call added as a final commit.

**Alternatives considered:**
1. Props + mapper now, wire later (chosen): add `OidcLoginButton` (`{ id, displayName }`) and `toOidcLoginButtons(providers, { signup })`, which filters by `allowSignup` and drops every other field; `server/lib/auth/login/getServerSideProps.tsx` and `lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx` pass the result; the input type temporarily copies the shape of #136's `OidcProviderPublicDto`.
2. Stack on #136's branch: import the real DTO and `getOidcProviderRepository()` and call `findEnabled()` in the server props from the start.
3. Fetch on the client: add a public tRPC query or API route that returns the button list and load it in the views on mount.

**Rationale:** It lets the PR open and be tested today without waiting for #136, which has no branch yet, and the mapper is a `.ts` unit that tests acceptance criteria 3–5 directly. Stacking is blocked on #136, and a client fetch adds a new public endpoint and a layout shift for no benefit.

**Consequences:** Easier: an independent, small PR with unit-tested filtering and field stripping. Harder: the temporary input type must be replaced with #136's DTO and the `findEnabled()` call added after #136 merges (recorded under Tech Debt → Introduced); until then no buttons appear on any instance.

### Decision 3: Naming the failed provider in messages

**Decision:** Use generic, translated failure messages that do not name the provider (for example "The sign-in provider could not be reached. Try again later or use another sign-in method.").

**Alternatives considered:**
1. Generic messages (chosen): fixed translation keys with no provider name, for every code on the login page and `/auth/error`.
2. Use the last-used value: the login view reads `lastUsed` (`useLastUsed.tsx`, localStorage) and, if it is `oidc-<id>`, fills in that provider's `displayName` from the `oidcProviders` prop.
3. Provider parameter from sub-issue 5: the `signIn` callback adds `&provider=oidc-<id>` to its custom `/auth/error` codes (as `[REDACTED:generic-password]-provider` already does, `next-auth-options.ts:1078`), and the error page looks up the display name on the server.

**Rationale:** It keeps this PR independent of sub-issue 5 and is the simplest option that is always correct. NextAuth's built-in redirects carry only `error` and `callbackUrl` (`next-auth/core/index.js:167-169`), so no option can name the provider for `OAuthSignin`/`OAuthCallback` reliably; the last-used value can name the [REDACTED:generic-password] provider.

**Consequences:** Easier: no coordination with sub-issue 5, no database lookup on the error page, simple tests. Harder: feature-spec criteria 22 and 23 ("We could not reach <display name>") are only partly met; adding provider names later is recorded under Tech Debt → Introduced.
```

```text
export function useLastUsed() {
  const [lastUsed, setLastUsed] = useState<LoginType>();

  useEffect(() => {
    const storedValue = localStorage.getItem("last_cal_login");
    if (storedValue) {
      setLastUsed(storedValue as LoginType);
    }
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (lastUsed) {
      localStorage.setItem("last_cal_login", lastUsed);
    } else {
      localStorage.removeItem("last_cal_login");
    }
  }, [lastUsed]);

  return [lastUsed, setLastUsed] as const;
```

## 3) Where the button type lives (the "two packages" point)

"Two packages" isn't a course requirement. I put that badly. Here's the actual concern:

- **The team rule on multiple packages.** CLAUDE.md lists "Changes affecting multiple packages" under **Ask first**. It doesn't forbid them. This PR already has to touch two packages:
  - `apps/web` for the code;
  - `packages/i18n` for the strings, which is unavoidable.

  Putting the type in `packages/lib/dto/` would add a third.
- **The team rule pointing the other way.** `data-dto-boundaries.md` says "All DTOs go in `packages/lib/dto/`".

  The DTOs there today, like `FeatureDto.ts`, are Zod schemas for data that repositories return. They're used by repositories and services in `packages/features`, for example `packages/features/flags/repositories/PrismaFeatureRepository.ts` (**Confirmed**). The rule is about stopping database types from leaking out of that layer.
- **What our type is.** `OidcLoginButton` (`{ id, displayName }`) is a view model for two web pages. It never goes into or out of a repository. The real data DTO, `OidcProviderPublicDto`, will be in `packages/lib/dto/OidcProviderDto.ts` because #136 creates it (#136's likely-files list).
- **A practical risk.** If I also add a file under `packages/lib/dto/`, especially one named like `OidcProviderDto.ts`, it could conflict with #136 when that merges.

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| Keep the type in `apps/web/modules/auth/lib/oidcLoginButtons.ts` (plan) | One fewer package. Sits next to the function that builds it. No conflict with #136 | A reviewer may point to the "all DTOs go in `packages/lib/dto`" rule. The PR should explain why |
| Put it in `packages/lib/dto/OidcLoginButtonDto.ts` | Follows the rule literally | A third package (an Ask-first item). Brushes against #136's file. Turns a page-only type into a shared one |

Both work; it's your call. If you keep the plan, I'll add a one-line note to the PR.

## 4) The existing `continue_with` key

- **Text:** `"Continue with {{appName}}"` (`common.json:425`).
- **Where it's used:** one place, `apps/web/modules/bookings/components/OverlayCalendar/OverlayCalendarContinueModal.tsx:30`, as `t("continue_with", { appName: APP_NAME })`. That's the booking page's "Continue with Cal.diy" prompt for showing your own calendar over the slots (**Confirmed**).
- **Translations:** it exists in all 37 locale files.
- **Related keys:** the sign-in buttons use separate keys: `continue_with_google`, `continue_with_microsoft` (`:1397`, `:3178`) and `continue_with_email`.

What changes depending on the choice:

| | Reuse `continue_with` | New `continue_with_provider` (`"Continue with {{providerName}}"`) |
|---|---|---|
| Other languages | Translated in all 37 locales immediately | English only until translators add it. Other locales fall back to English |
| Coupling | Tied to the booking modal. If someone rewords that modal (say "Continue to {{appName}}"), the sign-in buttons change too | Independent |
| Meaning | The placeholder is called `appName`, but you'd pass a provider name. It works, but reads oddly | Placeholder name matches its meaning, like the other sign-in keys |
| Spec | AC1 names `continue_with_provider`, so AC1 would need editing after the teammate review | Matches AC1 as written |
| Diff | 0 new lines | +1 line in `common.json` |

In practice what users see is the same in English. The real differences are other languages now versus independence from the booking modal later.

## 5) Sign-up stays in this PR

Done: step 6 stays, and I've noted it in the plan. That puts the PR at about 10 code files, right at the limit.

```typescript
import { IdentityProvider } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";

export type Translate = (key: string, options?: Record<string, string>) => string;

// NextAuth sends these codes back to the sign-in page as `?error=`; every other code goes to `/auth/error`.
const LOGIN_ERROR_KEYS = new Map<string, string>([
  ["OAuthSignin", "auth_error_provider_unreachable"],
  ["OAuthCallback", "auth_error_sign_in_failed"],
  ["Callback", "auth_error_sign_in_failed"],
]);

const ERROR_PAGE_KEYS = new Map<string, string>([
  ["user-creation-error", "user_creation_error"],
  ["saml-idp-not-authoritative", "saml_idp_not_authoritative_error"],
  ["unverified-email", "unverified_email_oauth_error"],
  ["AccessDenied", "auth_error_access_denied"],
  ["missing-email", "auth_error_missing_email"],
  ["oidc-signup-not-allowed", "auth_error_oidc_signup_not_allowed"],
  ["oidc-account-exists", "auth_error_oidc_account_exists"],
  ["unknown-provider", "auth_error_unknown_provider"],
]);

// #136 adds OIDC to IdentityProvider; compared as a string so this works before that lands.
const OIDC_IDENTITY_PROVIDER = "OIDC";

export function getLoginErrorMessage(t: Translate, error: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (!error) return null;
  return t(LOGIN_ERROR_KEYS.get(error) ?? "auth_error_sign_in_generic");
}

function getProviderName(t: Translate, provider: string | undefined): string {
  switch (provider) {
    case IdentityProvider.GOOGLE:
      return "Google";
    case IdentityProvider.CAL:
      return "Email and Password";
    case IdentityProvider.SAML:
      return "SAML (like Okta)";
    case OIDC_IDENTITY_PROVIDER:
      return t("single_sign_on");
    default:
      return "your original login method";
  }
}

export function getAuthErrorPageMessage(
  t: Translate,
  error: string | undefined,
  provider: string | undefined
): string {
  if (error === "[REDACTED:generic-password]-provider") {
    return t("account_managed_by_identity_provider_error", { provider: getProviderName(t, provider) });
  }
  const key = error ? ERROR_PAGE_KEYS.get(error) : undefined;
  if (key) return t(key);
  return t("error_during_login") + (error ? ` Error code: ${error}` : "");
}

```

```typescript
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import type { Translate } from "./authErrorMessages";
import { getAuthErrorPageMessage, getLoginErrorMessage } from "./authErrorMessages";

// Echoes the key (and options) so each test can see exactly which translation was requested.
const t: Translate = (key, options) => (options ? `${key}|${JSON.stringify(options)}` : key);

describe("getLoginErrorMessage", () => {
  it.each([
    ["OAuthSignin", "auth_error_provider_unreachable"],
    ["OAuthCallback", "auth_error_sign_in_failed"],
    ["Callback", "auth_error_sign_in_failed"],
  ])("maps %s to %s", (code, key) => {
    expect(getLoginErrorMessage(t, code)).toBe(key);
  });

  it.each(["OAuthCreateAccount", "OAuthAccountNotLinked", "SomethingNew"])(
    "falls back to the generic message for %s",
    (code) => {
      expect(getLoginErrorMessage(t, code)).toBe("auth_error_sign_in_generic");
    }
  );

  it("never echoes the raw code, even for names on Object.prototype", () => {
    expect(getLoginErrorMessage(t, "constructor")).toBe("auth_error_sign_in_generic");
    expect(getLoginErrorMessage(t, "<script>alert(1)</script>")).toBe("auth_error_sign_in_generic");
  });

  it.each([null, undefined, ""])("returns null (no alert) when error is %j", (error) => {
    expect(getLoginErrorMessage(t, error)).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe("getAuthErrorPageMessage", () => {
  it.each([
    ["AccessDenied", "auth_error_access_denied"],
    ["missing-email", "auth_error_missing_email"],
    ["oidc-signup-not-allowed", "auth_error_oidc_signup_not_allowed"],
    ["oidc-account-exists", "auth_error_oidc_account_exists"],
    ["unknown-provider", "auth_error_unknown_provider"],
  ])("maps the new code %s to %s", (code, key) => {
    expect(getAuthErrorPageMessage(t, code, undefined)).toBe(key);
  });

  it.each([
    ["user-creation-error", "user_creation_error"],
    ["saml-idp-not-authoritative", "saml_idp_not_authoritative_error"],
    ["unverified-email", "unverified_email_oauth_error"],
  ])("keeps the existing message for %s", (code, key) => {
    expect(getAuthErrorPageMessage(t, code, undefined)).toBe(key);
  });

  it("names OIDC accounts as single sign-on in [REDACTED:generic-password]-provider", () => {
    expect(getAuthErrorPageMessage(t, "[REDACTED:generic-password]-provider", "OIDC")).toBe(
      'account_managed_by_identity_provider_error|{"provider":"single_sign_on"}'
    );
  });

  it.each([
    ["GOOGLE", "Google"],
    ["CAL", "Email and Password"],
    ["SAML", "SAML (like Okta)"],
    ["AZUREAD", "your original login method"],
    [undefined, "your original login method"],
  ])("keeps the existing [REDACTED:generic-password]-provider name for %s", (provider, name) => {
    expect(getAuthErrorPageMessage(t, "[REDACTED:generic-password]-provider", provider)).toBe(
      `account_managed_by_identity_provider_error|${JSON.stringify({ provider: name })}`
    );
  });

  it("keeps the generic message with the error code for unknown codes", () => {
    expect(getAuthErrorPageMessage(t, "new-email-conflict", undefined)).toBe(
      "error_during_login Error code: new-email-conflict"
    );
    expect(getAuthErrorPageMessage(t, "constructor", undefined)).toBe(
      "error_during_login Error code: constructor"
    );
  });

  it("shows the generic message without a code when there is no error", () => {
    expect(getAuthErrorPageMessage(t, undefined, undefined)).toBe("error_during_login");
  });
});
```

Step 1 is done: the shared error-message module, its tests and the English strings. The tests pass and Biome is clean. The type check for `@calcom/web` is still running; I'll report its result when it finishes.

## What changed

**1. New file `apps/web/modules/auth/lib/authErrorMessages.ts` (57 lines)**
- Two lookup tables (`Map`s):
  - `LOGIN_ERROR_KEYS` (`:6-10`): `OAuthSignin` → `auth_error_provider_unreachable`; `OAuthCallback` and `Callback` → `auth_error_sign_in_failed`.
  - `ERROR_PAGE_KEYS` (`:12-21`): the three codes the error page already handles, plus `AccessDenied`, `missing-email`, `oidc-signup-not-allowed`, `oidc-account-exists` and `unknown-provider`.
- `getLoginErrorMessage(t, error)` (`:26-29`):
  ```ts
  if (!error) return null;
  return t(LOGIN_ERROR_KEYS.get(error) ?? "auth_error_sign_in_generic");
  ```
- `getProviderName(t, provider)` (`:31-44`): the existing names for `GOOGLE`, `CAL` and `SAML`, plus `"OIDC"` → `t("single_sign_on")`.
- `getAuthErrorPageMessage(t, error, provider)` (`:46-57`): handles `[REDACTED:generic-password]-provider` first, then the lookup table, then today's fallback, `error_during_login` plus "Error code: …".

**2. New file `apps/web/modules/auth/lib/authErrorMessages.test.ts` (84 lines, 26 tests).**

**3. `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`:** 9 new keys, added just above the `ADD_NEW_STRINGS_ABOVE_THIS_LINE…` marker (now `:4847-4855`). These are the 8 `auth_error_*` messages and `single_sign_on`.

## Why
Design decision 1: one mapping that both pages use and that Vitest can reach. Vitest only collects `.ts`/`.js` test files under `apps/**` (`vitest.workspace.ts:59`).

This covers AC6, AC7 and AC8 as logic, and the English-strings part of AC9. No page uses the module yet; steps 2 and 3 connect it.

## Assumptions
- **`t` is passed in** rather than the module returning a key. That keeps two things inside tested code: the nested "single sign-on" translation and the "Error code" suffix. The pages will pass a small wrapper, `(key, opts) => t(key, opts)`.
- **`"OIDC"` is compared as a string**, because `IdentityProvider` has no `OIDC` value yet (`schema.prisma:367-372`). Step 7 switches it to the enum after #136 merges.
- **The message wording is my draft.** Please read the 9 strings in `common.json`. Changing the wording doesn't affect the tests, which check keys only.
- **`continue_with_provider` moves to step 5**, where it's first used.

## How it relates to existing code
- `getAuthErrorPageMessage` copies the existing if/else chain in `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/auth/error/page.tsx:36-56` (**Confirmed**), including the hard-coded English provider names. Step 2 replaces that chain with this function.
- The login-page codes come from NextAuth's sign-in redirect list (`node_modules/next-auth/core/index.js:209-214`). `AccessDenied` is on the error page because NextAuth sends it there (`core/routes/callback.js:85`) (**Confirmed**).
- `unknown-provider` is the code the app already sends from `next-auth-options.ts:861` (**Confirmed**).

## What could go [REDACTED:generic-password]
- **Lookups with odd codes.** A plain object lookup such as `KEYS["constructor"]` would return a built-in function instead of `undefined`. Using `Map` avoids that, and a test covers it.
- **The raw code still appears on `/auth/error`** for unknown codes ("Error code: …"). That's existing behaviour, kept on purpose. React escapes it, so it's text, not HTML.
- **If sub-issue 5 uses different code names** (say `oidc_signup_not_allowed`), those errors fall through to the generic message. The names come from the spec; confirm them with whoever takes sub-issue 5.
- **Other languages** show the English text until translators add the keys.

## Tests and what they prove
The expected values come from AC6–8, not from the code's own output.

| Test | Proves |
|---|---|
| `maps %s to %s` (3) | AC6 login codes map to the right keys |
| `falls back to the generic message` (3) | Any other code shows the generic message (AC6) |
| `never echoes the raw code` | `constructor` and an HTML string give the generic message (AC6: "the raw error value is never shown") |
| `returns null (no alert)` (3) | No alert when there's no `?error=` (AC6) |

| `names OIDC accounts as single sign-on` | AC8 |
| `keeps the existing [REDACTED:generic-password]-provider name` (5) | `GOOGLE`, `CAL`, `SAML`, `AZUREAD` and no provider are unchanged (AC8) |
| unknown code / no error (2) | The existing fallback, including "Error code: …", is unchanged |

Design decision 1 says both pages share one tested mapping. This step makes the error page show the new AC7 messages (`AccessDenied`, `missing-email`, `oidc-signup-not-allowed`, `oidc-account-exists`, `unknown-provider`) and the AC8 "single sign-on" name.

- **The `(key, options) => t(key, options)` wrapper.** `getTranslate()` returns i18next's `TFunction`, which has many overloads and doesn't directly match the module's simpler `Translate` type. The wrapper satisfies it, and the type check confirms it.

```typescript
// Mirrors the fields this file needs from #136's OidcProviderPublicDto (packages/lib/dto/OidcProviderDto.ts).
// Replace with that type once #136 merges.
export type OidcProviderForLogin = {
  id: string;
  displayName: string;
  allowSignup: boolean;
};

export type OidcLoginButton = {
  id: string;
  displayName: string;
};

export type OidcSignInProviderId = `oidc-${string}`;

export function getOidcSignInProviderId(id: string): OidcSignInProviderId {
  return `oidc-${id}`;
}

// Copies only id and displayName: the full DTO also has issuer, clientId, scopes and
// allowedDomains, which must not be serialized into page props sent to the browser.
function toButton(provider: OidcProviderForLogin): OidcLoginButton {
  return { id: provider.id, displayName: provider.displayName };
}

export function toOidcLoginButtons(providers: OidcProviderForLogin[]): OidcLoginButton[] {
  return providers.map(toButton);
}

export function toOidcSignupButtons(
  providers: OidcProviderForLogin[],
  { signupDisabled }: { signupDisabled: boolean }
): OidcLoginButton[] {
  if (signupDisabled) return [];
  return providers.filter((provider) => provider.allowSignup).map(toButton);
}

```

```typescript
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import type { OidcProviderForLogin } from "./oidcLoginButtons";
import { getOidcSignInProviderId, toOidcLoginButtons, toOidcSignupButtons } from "./oidcLoginButtons";

// Shaped like #136's OidcProviderPublicDto, including the fields that must never reach the browser.
const acme = {
  id: "cl_acme",
  displayName: "Acme SSO",
  allowSignup: true,
  issuer: "https://acme.example.com",
  clientId: "acme-client",
  scopes: "openid email profile",
  allowedDomains: ["acme.com"],
};
const partner = {
  id: "cl_partner",
  displayName: "Partner Login",
  allowSignup: false,
  issuer: "https://partner.example.com",
  clientId: "partner-client",
  scopes: "openid email",
  allowedDomains: [],
};
const providers: OidcProviderForLogin[] = [acme, partner];

describe("toOidcLoginButtons", () => {
  it("returns one button per provider in the given (admin) order", () => {
    expect(toOidcLoginButtons(providers)).toEqual([
      { id: "cl_acme", displayName: "Acme SSO" },
      { id: "cl_partner", displayName: "Partner Login" },
    ]);
  });

  it("keeps only id and displayName", () => {
    for (const button of toOidcLoginButtons(providers)) {
      expect(Object.keys(button).sort()).toEqual(["displayName", "id"]);
    }
  });

  it("returns no buttons when no provider is enabled", () => {
    expect(toOidcLoginButtons([])).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe("toOidcSignupButtons", () => {
  it("shows only providers that allow new accounts", () => {
    expect(toOidcSignupButtons(providers, { signupDisabled: false })).toEqual([
      { id: "cl_acme", displayName: "Acme SSO" },
    ]);
  });

  it("keeps the admin order among providers that allow new accounts", () => {
    const second = { ...acme, id: "cl_second", displayName: "Second SSO" };
    expect(toOidcSignupButtons([second, partner, acme], { signupDisabled: false })).toEqual([
      { id: "cl_second", displayName: "Second SSO" },
      { id: "cl_acme", displayName: "Acme SSO" },
    ]);
  });

  it("keeps only id and displayName", () => {
    for (const button of toOidcSignupButtons(providers, { signupDisabled: false })) {
      expect(Object.keys(button).sort()).toEqual(["displayName", "id"]);
    }
  });

  it("shows no buttons when sign-up is disabled site-wide", () => {
    expect(toOidcSignupButtons(providers, { signupDisabled: true })).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("returns no buttons when no provider is enabled", () => {
    expect(toOidcSignupButtons([], { signupDisabled: false })).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe("getOidcSignInProviderId", () => {
  it("builds the NextAuth provider id oidc-<id>", () => {
    expect(getOidcSignInProviderId("cl_acme")).toBe("oidc-cl_acme");
  });
});

```

Steps 3–6 are done, so everything that can be built before #136 is finished. Step 7 (loading providers from the database) is still blocked on #136. The type check on `@calcom/web` passes with 0 errors after I fixed one error, and all 35 unit tests pass.

**Nothing visible changes on the login or sign-up pages yet.** Both server props pass an empty provider list until #136 merges. The button rendering is unit-tested underneath, but nobody has seen it on screen.

## What changed

**Step 3: the login page shows `?error=` messages (AC6)**
- `apps/web/modules/auth/login-view.tsx`:
  - stores the `?error=` code in a new state value, `signInErrorCode`;
  - turns it into a message with `getLoginErrorMessage` from step 1 when the page renders;
  - clears it when the email/password form is submitted, so an old OAuth error doesn't stay on screen.
- A credentials error still takes priority over the URL error.

**Step 4: building the button list (AC3, AC4, AC5)**
- New file `apps/web/modules/auth/lib/oidcLoginButtons.ts`:
  - `toOidcLoginButtons` for the login page.
  - `toOidcSignupButtons(…, { signupDisabled })` for the sign-up page.
  - Both copy only `id` and `displayName`, so the other provider fields never reach the browser.
  - `getOidcSignInProviderId(id)` builds the `oidc-<id>` id that NextAuth will use.
- New file `oidcLoginButtons.test.ts` (9 tests).
- `useLastUsed.tsx:7`: the "last used" type now also accepts `oidc-<id>`.

**Step 5: login buttons (AC1, AC2)**
- `server/lib/auth/login/getServerSideProps.tsx`: `const enabledOidcProviders: OidcProviderForLogin[] = []`, passed through as `oidcProviders`. Step 7 replaces the `[]` with `findEnabled()`, a one-line change.
- `login-view.tsx`:
  - one "Continue with …" button per provider, after Microsoft. Clicking it sets "last used" and calls `signIn("oidc-<id>", { callbackUrl })`, and the button shows the Last used badge.
  - `showSocialLogin` is now also true when there are OIDC providers, so on a site with only OIDC configured the buttons and the "or" divider still appear.

**Step 6: sign-up buttons (AC4)**
- `lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx`: `oidcProviders` honours the site-wide sign-up switches, `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_SIGNUP` and `disable-signup`. That matters because invite links with a token still render the sign-up page when the env var is set (`:65`).
- `signup-view.tsx`: the buttons go after Microsoft and use `signIn` with `redirectUrl`. The divider condition now includes OIDC.

**Translation:** `continue_with_provider` ("Continue with {{providerName}}") added to `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`.

## Assumptions
- **The temporary provider type** copies the shape of #136's DTO (`id`, `displayName`, `allowSignup`). If #136 names these differently, step 7 adjusts.
- **The provider id is `oidc-<id>`**, per the agreement with sub-issue 5.

## What could go [REDACTED:generic-password]
- **The rendered buttons haven't been seen.** The list is empty until #136, so nothing appears in the app yet. The filtering and field stripping are unit-tested, but the button markup isn't.
- **Sign-up username features.** OIDC sign-ups skip username prefill and the premium-username check (Tech Debt → Introduced, as agreed).
- **Provider names in the "last used" value.** A deleted provider's `oidc-<id>` can stay in localStorage. It's harmless: no button matches it, so no badge shows.

## Tests (35 in total, all passing)
The new `oidcLoginButtons.test.ts` checks:
- the admin order is kept;
- each button has exactly the keys `id` and `displayName`, using test data shaped like #136's DTO with `issuer`, `clientId`, `scopes` and `allowedDomains` (AC5);
- the sign-up page shows only providers that allow new accounts, in admin order;
- no buttons when sign-up is disabled (AC4);
- an empty provider list gives no buttons (AC3);
- the `oidc-<id>` format.

```typescript
import { fireEvent, render, screen, within } from "@testing-library/react";
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import type { PageProps } from "./login-view";
import Login from "./login-view";

const mocks = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  searchParams: new URLSearchParams(),
  signIn: vi.fn(),
}));

vi.mock("next-auth/react", () => ({
  signIn: mocks.signIn,
}));

vi.mock("@calcom/lib/hooks/useCompatSearchParams", () => ({
  useCompatSearchParams: () => mocks.searchParams,
}));

// Echoes the key and options so assertions can name the exact translation the page asked for.
vi.mock("@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale", () => ({
  useLocale: () => ({
    t: (key: string, options?: Record<string, string>) =>
      options ? `${key}|${JSON.stringify(options)}` : key,
  }),
}));

// Not under test, and they pull in PWA and 2FA dependencies.
vi.mock("@components/AddToHomescreen", () => ({ default: () => null }));
vi.mock("@components/auth/TwoFactor", () => ({ default: () => null }));
vi.mock("@components/auth/BackupCode", () => ({ default: () => null }));

const acme = { id: "cl_acme", displayName: "Acme SSO" };
const partner = { id: "cl_partner", displayName: "Partner Login" };
const continueWith = (name: string) => `continue_with_provider|${JSON.stringify({ providerName: name })}`;

function renderLogin(props: Partial<PageProps> = {}) {
  const defaults: PageProps = {
    csrfToken: "csrf",
    isGoogleLoginEnabled: false,
    isOutlookLoginEnabled: false,
    oidcProviders: [],
    totpEmail: null,
  };
  return render(<Login {...defaults} {...props} />);
}

beforeEach(() => {
  mocks.searchParams = new URLSearchParams();
  window.localStorage.clear();
});

describe("Login page: ?error= messages (AC6)", () => {
  it.each([
    ["OAuthSignin", "auth_error_provider_unreachable"],
    ["Callback", "auth_error_sign_in_failed"],
    ["SomethingNew", "auth_error_sign_in_generic"],
  ])("shows the translated message for ?error=%s", (code, key) => {
    mocks.searchParams = new URLSearchParams({ error: code });
    renderLogin();
    expect(screen.getByText(key)).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("does not show the raw error code", () => {
    mocks.searchParams = new URLSearchParams({ error: "SomethingNew" });
    renderLogin();
    expect(screen.queryByText(/SomethingNew/)).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("shows no sign-in error without ?error=", () => {
    renderLogin();
    expect(screen.queryByText(/^auth_error_/)).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});

describe("Login page: OIDC buttons", () => {
  it("shows one button per provider, in the given order, after Google (AC1)", () => {
    renderLogin({ isGoogleLoginEnabled: true, oidcProviders: [acme, partner] });
    const buttons = screen.getAllByRole("button").map((button) => button.getAttribute("data-testid"));
    const order = buttons.filter((id) => id === "google" || id?.startsWith("oidc-"));
    expect(order).toEqual(["google", "oidc-cl_acme", "oidc-cl_partner"]);
    expect(screen.getByTestId("oidc-cl_acme")).toHaveTextContent(continueWith("Acme SSO"));
    expect(screen.getByTestId("oidc-cl_partner")).toHaveTextContent(continueWith("Partner Login"));
  });

  it("starts the oidc-<id> flow and records it as last used on click (AC1)", () => {
    renderLogin({ oidcProviders: [acme] });
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByTestId("oidc-cl_acme"));
    expect(mocks.signIn).toHaveBeenCalledWith("oidc-cl_acme", { callbackUrl: expect.any(String) });
    expect(window.localStorage.getItem("last_cal_login")).toBe("oidc-cl_acme");
  });

  it("shows the Last used badge on the provider used last time (AC1)", () => {
    window.localStorage.setItem("last_cal_login", "oidc-cl_partner");
    renderLogin({ oidcProviders: [acme, partner] });
    expect(within(screen.getByTestId("oidc-cl_partner")).getByText("last_used")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(within(screen.getByTestId("oidc-cl_acme")).queryByText("last_used")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("shows the buttons and the divider when only OIDC is enabled (AC2)", () => {
    renderLogin({ oidcProviders: [acme] });
    expect(screen.getByTestId("oidc-cl_acme")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText("or")).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("looks as before with no providers: no OIDC buttons and no divider (AC3)", () => {
    renderLogin();
    expect(screen.queryByTestId(/^oidc-/)).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByText("or")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});

```

The e2e failures aren't caused by our branch: MailHog, the local email server the tests use, isn't running. I've corrected the [REDACTED:generic-password] claim and added the login-page test (10 tests, all passing). The new test puts the PR over the 10-file limit.

## E2E failures: MailHog isn't running
- **Cause:** `.env:257` has `E2E_TEST_MAILHOG_ENABLED=1`, but nothing is listening on `localhost:8025`.
- **How it fails:** after each test that creates users, the cleanup `users.deleteAll()` asks MailHog for those users' emails (`apps/web/playwright/fixtures/users.ts:555-566`). The connection is refused and throws the empty `AggregateError` every failure shows.
- **Why these tests:** all 7 failures, including "Should warn when password is incorrect", create users with the `users` fixture. "Should warn when user does not exist" and the sign-up-through-the-UI tests don't, and they passed. The "Username is taken" screenshot shows the sign-up form working normally.
- **Fix** (from `students.md:54-55`):
  ```bash
  cd packages/emails && docker compose up -d && cd ../..   # start MailHog on 8025/1025
  ```
  Then re-run, for example `PLAYWRIGHT_HEADLESS=1 yarn e2e apps/web/playwright/login.e2e.ts`, followed by `signup.e2e.ts` and `auth/`. If anything still fails with MailHog up, send me the output.

The [REDACTED:generic-password] claim was that Vitest never runs `.tsx` tests under `apps/**`. It does run them from `apps/web/modules/**` and `apps/web/components/**` (`vitest.workspace.ts:158`, `:188`). Only pages under `apps/web/app/**`, such as `/auth/error`, have no test project. Fixed in:

The old version is kept as `design.v1.md`. **If you pasted `## Design` into the issue, update that Rationale paragraph there too.**

## New test: `apps/web/modules/auth/login-view.test.tsx` (114 lines, 10 tests)
- **How it works:** it renders the real login page with these replaced by stand-ins:
  - `next-auth/react` (`signIn`), `next/navigation`, `useCompatSearchParams` and `useLocale`. The stand-in `t` returns the key plus its parameters, so the tests can check exactly which text was requested;
  - three components that aren't under test.

| AC | What it checks |
|---|---|
| 6 | `?error=OAuthSignin`, `Callback` and an unknown code each show the right message. The raw code is never shown. No error message without `?error=` |
| 1 | The buttons appear in the given order after Google, with the "Continue with …" label. Clicking calls `signIn("oidc-cl_acme", { callbackUrl })` and stores `oidc-cl_acme` as last used. The Last used badge appears only on the matching provider |
| 2 | With only OIDC enabled, the buttons and the "or" divider appear |
| 3 | With no providers: no OIDC buttons and no divider |

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 21:35:54Z)**_

Here's what happened, using the actual commits on your branch.

## Before: two lines of work from one starting point

You created your branch from `main` at `ed1fa24572` (the merge of PR #140). From there, two things happened independently:

```
                 e71ed02  5a45d29  50151a7  55ad016  650b29e  342763c   ← your branch (6 commits)
                /
ed1fa24572 ────
                \
                 4e95592 … 8fe6223 ── be93db6   ← origin/main (PR #144, "running late", 10 commits)
```

- Your 6 commits only existed on your machine.
- Your teammate's 10 commits (PR #144) were on GitHub. Your computer didn't know about them yet.

`ed1fa24572` is the **merge base**, the last commit both lines share (**Confirmed** with `git merge-base`).

## What `git fetch origin` did

It downloaded the commits from GitHub that you didn't have and moved your **remote-tracking refs**, such as `origin/main`, to point at them. Remote-tracking refs are your local bookmarks for "where GitHub's branches are".

- It **did not change your branch, your files or your working tree**. `feat/issue-146-oidc-login-buttons` still pointed at `342763c`.
- Your local copy of `origin/main` moved from `ed1fa24572` to `be93db6`. That's why `pr-facts` then said "10 behind".

Fetch is always safe: it only updates your view of the remote.

## What `git merge origin/main` did

It created a new commit, `5ea0436`, with **two parents**:
1. your previous tip, `342763c`;
2. main's tip, `be93db6`.

```
                 e71ed02 … 342763c ──────────┐
                /                             \
ed1fa24572 ────                                5ea0436   ← your branch now (HEAD)
                \                             /
                 4e95592 … 8fe6223 ── be93db6            ← origin/main
```

That's the shape `git log --graph` shows: the `*   5ea04364e4` line at the top, with two lines coming out of it.

To build that commit's files, Git did a **three-way merge**. It compared three versions of each file: the merge base `ed1fa24572`, your tip and main's tip.
- **Files only one side changed** were taken from that side automatically. That's the 30 staged files you saw (the running-late feature, AI logs, the Stryker setup).
- **`common.json` was changed by both sides in the same place**, right after `waitlist_join_time`. Git couldn't decide the order, so it paused and left the conflict markers for you. "Accept Both Changes", then `git add` and `git commit`, completed the merge commit with your resolution.

How your history was affected:
- **Nothing was rewritten.** Your 6 commits keep their hashes (`e71ed02` … `342763c`). The merge only *added* one commit on top.
- That's the main difference from a **rebase**. A rebase would replay your 6 commits on top of `be93db6` as 6 new commits with new hashes, giving a straight line but a rewritten history. Since your branch isn't on GitHub yet, either would have been fine. A merge is the safe default because it never rewrites commits.
- Your branch now contains all of `main`, so it's "0 behind".

## What happens when you push

Your branch **isn't on GitHub yet** (`git ls-remote` finds no `feat/issue-146-oidc-login-buttons` there). So `git push -u origin feat/issue-146-oidc-login-buttons` will:

1. **Upload only the commits GitHub doesn't have.** That's your 6 commits and the merge commit, 7 in total. Main's 10 commits are already on GitHub, so they aren't sent again; the merge commit just refers to them by hash.
2. **Create the branch on GitHub** pointing at `5ea0436`.
3. With `-u`, **link your local branch to it**. From then on, a plain `git push` / `git pull` knows where to go, and `git status` shows "ahead/behind origin/feat/…".

It **does not touch `main` on GitHub.** `main` only changes when the PR is merged.

## How this shows up in the PR

GitHub shows a PR as the difference between `main` and your branch, measured from their merge base.
- After your merge, that base is now `be93db6`, main's current tip.
- So the PR's **"Files changed" shows only your 12 files**. The 30 running-late files don't appear, because `main` already has them.
- The **Commits** tab lists your 6 commits plus the merge commit.

When the PR is later merged into `main`, `main` gains your commits and, depending on the merge button the team uses, a merge commit or one squashed commit. Either way, the conflict you resolved won't come back, because your branch already contains main's version of `common.json`.

## Why it was worth doing before opening the PR
- **The conflict was resolved by you**, the person who knows both sets of strings, not by whoever clicks "Merge" later.
- **Your tests and type check ran against the combined code.** The checks I just ran (56 tests, 0 type errors) show your change works with #144's changes, not only with the older `main`.
- **Reviewers see a PR that can merge cleanly.** GitHub would otherwise show "This branch has conflicts that must be resolved".

```markdown
## What does this PR do?

Closes #146

Sub-issue 6 of #131 (OIDC sign-in). Adds the login and sign-up buttons for admin-configured OIDC providers and makes sign-in failures visible. It depends on #136 for the provider data: until #136 merges, both pages receive an empty provider list, so **nothing changes on screen except the error messages** (see Tech Debt).

### What changed

- **Shared error-message mapping:** `apps/web/modules/auth/lib/authErrorMessages.ts`
  - `getLoginErrorMessage` (`:26`) maps NextAuth's sign-in-page codes: `OAuthSignin` → provider unreachable; `OAuthCallback` / `Callback` → sign-in failed; anything else → a generic message (`:6-10`).
  - `getAuthErrorPageMessage` (`:46`) holds the existing `/auth/error` messages unchanged, plus `AccessDenied`, `missing-email`, `oidc-signup-not-allowed`, `oidc-account-exists` and `unknown-provider` (`:12-21`). It names OIDC accounts as "single sign-on" in `[REDACTED:generic-password]-provider` (`:39`).
  - Lookups use `Map`, so a code like `constructor` can't match a built-in object property.
- **`/auth/error` uses the module:** `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/auth/error/page.tsx:36` replaces the old if/else chain.
- **The login page reads `?error=`:** `apps/web/modules/auth/login-view.tsx`
  - keeps the code in state (`:132`) and shows the translated message in the existing alert (`:181-182`, `:341-343`);
  - submitting the email form clears it;
  - this applies to Google and Microsoft failures too. Before, the page ignored `error` completely.
- **Provider-button mapping:** `apps/web/modules/auth/lib/oidcLoginButtons.ts`
  - `toOidcLoginButtons` (`:26`) and `toOidcSignupButtons` (`:30`) copy only `id` and `displayName` into page props;
  - the sign-up version keeps only providers with `allowSignup` and returns nothing when sign-up is disabled;
  - `getOidcSignInProviderId` (`:16`) builds the NextAuth id `oidc-<id>`.
- **Login buttons:**
  - `login-view.tsx:244-262`: one "Continue with <name>" button per provider, after Microsoft. Clicking it records `oidc-<id>` as last used and calls `signIn("oidc-<id>", { callbackUrl })`;
  - `showSocialLogin` (`:184`) now counts OIDC providers, so an instance with only OIDC configured still shows the buttons and the divider;
  - server props: `apps/web/server/lib/auth/login/getServerSideProps.tsx:90`, `:97`;
  - `useLastUsed.tsx:9` accepts `oidc-<id>`.
- **Sign-up buttons:**
  - `apps/web/modules/signup-view.tsx:737-751`, divider condition at `:754`;
  - server props: `apps/web/lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx:59-69`. These apply `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_SIGNUP` / `disable-signup` too, because invite links with a token still render the sign-up page when the env var is set.
- **Strings:** 10 keys in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:4847-4856`.

### Why

The login and sign-up pages could only show the hard-coded Google and Microsoft buttons, so users had no way to reach an OIDC provider. Sign-in failures were also invisible: NextAuth redirects failed OAuth sign-ins to `/auth/login?error=…` (`next-auth/core/index.js:209-214`), but `login-view.tsx` never read `error`.

This PR meets acceptance criteria 1–9 of #146. Criteria 1, 4 and 5 are fully visible only once #136 supplies real providers; the logic is tested now with sample data.
```

```bash
NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1 yarn workspace @calcom/web start -p 3000

# Terminal 2: seed, then every login/sign-up/auth spec in one run

PLAYWRIGHT_HEADLESS=1 yarn e2e apps/web/playwright/login.e2e.ts apps/web/playwright/login.oauth.e2e.ts apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts apps/web/playwright/signup.e2e.ts apps/web/playwright/auth/
```

Yes. CI has been failing because of how the repository and its CI setup are configured, not because of anyone's code changes. Almost all of the failures in the last three sprints come from two causes, and neither depends on what a PR changes.

## The main PR workflow ("PR Update")
Since Sep 13 there have been about 164 runs; 82 failed. I grouped the failures by the step that failed (**Confirmed** through the GitHub API):

| Cause | Failed runs | When | What happens |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Security audit finds critical vulnerabilities in dependencies** | 63 | Sep 14 – Nov 11 | `.github/workflows/security-audit.yml:18-19` runs `yarn npm audit --all --recursive --severity critical`. Packages in the lockfile have critical advisories: `next` (GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36, GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4), `handlebars` (GHSA-8r5x-fm3f-whwj, GHSA-p8wg-vrv2-v86f) and `@sentry/nextjs` (GHSA-mchm-gjx6-7h55). Every PR fails this check whatever it changes |
| **2. Playwright can't install on GitHub's new runner** | 19 (every run since Nov 12) | Nov 12 – now | `ubuntu-latest` is now Ubuntu 26.04, and the repo's Playwright 1.57.0 (`package.json:93`) doesn't support it: "*Playwright does not support chromium on ubuntu26.04-x64*". This happens in the **Prepare** job, so every later job is **skipped**: Linters, Type Checks, the 8 Tests jobs, Production builds. Then `required` fails. **At the moment CI runs no checks at all** |
| 3. Prisma migration check fails at "Set up job" | 10 | Sep 16 – Oct 30 | The log only shows "Please run `prisma generate`" during install. Exact cause **Unverified** |
| Real code failures | 4 | scattered | 3 unit-test runs and 1 type-check run. These are normal failures from individual PRs |

## Workflows that fail on every push
| Workflow | Cause |
|---|---|
| `i18n.yml`, `release-docker.yaml` | **The workflow files themselves are invalid.** They use `secrets.…` inside an `if:` (`i18n.yml:13`, `release-docker.yaml:109`, `:120`), which GitHub doesn't allow, so GitHub can't run them. It marks them failed on *every* push to *any* branch, even though they only run for `main` or tags. Your branch's two red marks are these |
| Delete, cleanup-report | `[@octokit/auth-app] appId option is required`. The fork doesn't have the upstream project's GitHub App secrets |
| Next.js Bundle Analysis | `Please set NEXTAUTH_SECRET`. The fork doesn't have that secret either |
| Validate PRs | Only fails when a PR title isn't a conventional commit, for example "Feat/issue 150 min cancellation notice backend". **Your title will pass** |

## What this means for your PR
- Once you open it, "PR Update" will fail at **Prepare** (cause 2), and no lint, type-check or test job will run. CI can't verify your PR either way.
- The course allows "CI passes (or manual verification documented)". Your draft already documents the local runs: 56/56 tests, 0 type errors, Biome, and E2E 15/0/3. I suggest replacing the CI line with:
  > **CI:** fails for reasons unrelated to this PR. Since 2026-11-12 the `Prepare` job can't install Playwright on GitHub's Ubuntu 26.04 runner ("Playwright does not support chromium on ubuntu26.04-x64"), so every lint, type-check and test job is skipped. The `i18n.yml` and `release-docker.yaml` failures are invalid workflow files (`secrets` used in `if:`). Verification was done locally, as listed below.

## Fixes (none of this is in your PR's scope)
1. **Playwright:**
   - pin the runner with `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` in `.github/workflows/pr.yml` and the Playwright install action (small change); or
   - upgrade `@playwright/test`. That's a dependency change; AGENTS.md says to ask first.
2. **Security audit:**
   - update `next`, `handlebars` and `@sentry/nextjs`, which needs the team's agreement and testing; or
   - make the critical-only audit non-blocking for the fork, which is a policy decision.
3. **Invalid workflows:** move the secret check into a job-level `env:` and test the env value, or disable those workflows in the fork.

These would make a good **optional hardening issue (D1)** for the team, and the sprint report's **Suite health** section (D8) could use these numbers.

```text
// Mutation testing for Sprint 3 (D6). Run it on the files your PR changed, never on the whole repo:
//   TZ=UTC yarn stryker run --mutate "path/to/file.ts"
// Set STRYKER_JSON to write the JSON report where the course wants it, for example
//   STRYKER_JSON=docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/130-zach-short-before.json
/** @type {import("@stryker-mutator/api/core").PartialStrykerOptions} */
export default {
  testRunner: "vitest",
  plugins: ["@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner"],
  vitest: {
    configFile: "vitest.config.mts",
    // Only the tests that import the mutated file run, which keeps a run to minutes in this monorepo.
    related: true,
  },
  // Not inPlace: in this repo the in-place backup lands inside the project, Vitest then collects the backup
  // copies, and the restore drops the executable bit on scripts. The sandbox copy avoids both. These folders
  // have no unit tests that features or web code import, so leaving them out keeps the copy small.
  // .claude and .cursor hold symlinks to folders, and packages/prisma/.env links to a root .env that may not
  // exist; the sandbox copy fails on all three.
  ignorePatterns: [
    "docs",
    "ai-logs",
    "specs",
    "apps/api/v2",
    "apps/web/public",
    "packages/embeds",
    "reports",
    ".claude",
    ".cursor",
    "packages/prisma/.env",
  ],
  ignoreStatic: true,
  concurrency: 4,
  timeoutMS: 30000,
  reporters: ["clear-text", "progress", "json", "html"],
  jsonReporter: { fileName: process.env.STRYKER_JSON ?? "reports/mutation/mutation.json" },
  htmlReporter: { fileName: "reports/mutation/mutation.html" },
};
```

```text
**Tool:** StrykerJS 10.1.1 with the Vitest runner

**Command** (Git Bash; Stryker 10 needs Node 22, and this machine's nvm has no `exec`):
`TZ=UTC STRYKER_JSON=docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/139-julissaehp-<before|after>.json "$LOCALAPPDATA/Author Software/nvm/installs/v22.23.5/node.exe" node_modules/@stryker-mutator/core/bin/stryker.js run stryker.139.config.mjs`
**Reports:** [before](reports/139-julissaehp-before.json) · [after](reports/139-julissaehp-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before 65.16% → after 79.03% (covered mutants only: 87.45% → 92.45%)
**Note:** line numbers below refer to commit `8222569`, the after run. Merging `main` later (#144) moved four of the
mutated ranges across two files without changing their code: `bookingActions.ts` 12–32 → 13–33 and 311–317 → 338–344, and
`BookingActionsDropdown.tsx` 72 → 74 and 240 → 246.

### Setup notes

- **Only the executable lines #139 added or changed are mutated: 313 mutants in 18 files.**
  - This covers both PRs: #142's settings UI, and the backend PR's persistence, enforcement, booking page and bookings list.
  - Imports produce no mutants, so they are left out, as are type-only lines, the `null` default in `defaultEvents.ts` and the test builder.
  - `schema.prisma`, `migration.sql` and `common.json` are also left out: Stryker can only mutate JavaScript and TypeScript.
  - `BookingListItem.tsx` and `BookingActionsDropdown.tsx` are in scope but produced 0 mutants. That's why the reports list 16 files.
- **The test list is explicit.**
  - The before run used the 8 test files written for #139 (175 tests).
  - The after run adds `BookingRepository.test.ts`, which holds the new repository tests, for 9 files and 191 tests. #140 also listed that file.
  - The mutated code did not change between the runs. Both reports contain the same 313 mutants at identical locations, checked by comparing file, position, mutator and replacement.
- **Stryker 10 requires Node 22 or newer**, and this machine's default is Node 20. Node 22 is called by its full path because this nvm has no `exec`.
  The command runs Stryker's `bin/stryker.js` directly, because `node_modules/.bin/stryker` is a shell shim that would start under the default Node 20.
- **`ignoreStatic` is on** (from the shared config). Values built when a module first loads are reported as Ignored in both runs: `MS_PER_MINUTE` and the error-code string in `minimumCancellationNotice.ts`, and the tRPC input schema.
- **The before run used merge commit `b3be818`, and the after run used `8222569`.** Only test files and the Vitest test list changed in between.
- **Credits:**
  - @zach-short: the shared config (#135); the `file:N-N` single-line form and leaving type-only lines out (#153).
```

| `apps/web/modules/signup-view.tsx` | 201, 737-754 | **no** (`signup-view.test.tsx` never passes `oidcProviders`) |

| `apps/web/server/lib/auth/login/getServerSideProps.tsx` and `apps/web/lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx` | 90, 97; 59-68 | **no** |
| `useLastUsed.tsx` | type-only change | produces no mutants |

- **Option A: only the code unit tests reach** (the first three rows). This is what kojoshuay's #137 did (`stryker.137.config.mjs:13-19`).
  - Pros: the score reflects how good the tests are, without any "No coverage" noise.
  - Cons: the signup buttons and the server-side wiring are never measured, and a grader may see that as narrowing the scope.
- **Option B: every executable line the PR changed** (all rows). This is what julissaehp's #139 did.
  - Pros: it's complete and honest, and the No-coverage mutants in `signup-view` give an obvious test gap to fix in the after run.
  - Cons: the before score is lower, the run is longer, and server files can be awkward to load under jsdom.

6. You commit everything on the PR branch: config, reports, doc and the new test.

Steps 1 to 3 are done, and the dry run succeeded: **3 files, 109 mutants, and all 45 tests passed** inside Stryker. You can do the official before run now.

## What I wrote, and the one fix I made along the way
- **`stryker.146.config.mjs`** builds on the shared config by zach-short. It mutates:
  - `authErrorMessages.ts` and `oidcLoginButtons.ts` in full;
  - the changed lines of `login-view.tsx`: 132-134, 162, 181-184, 244-264 and 341-343. I left out line 110 because it only destructures a prop and Stryker produces no mutants there.
- **`vitest.stryker-146.config.mts`** runs only the 3 test files for #146.
  - I first added `apps/web/modules/test-setup.ts` as a setup file, and that **broke all 10 `login-view` tests**. Its mock of `@calcom/lib/constants` has no `WEBAPP_URL`, which `login-view.tsx:153` uses.
  - With that file removed, **all 45 tests pass**. The comment in the config now explains why it isn't loaded.
- **Assumption:** the line ranges only hold for the current code. If `login-view.tsx` changes, they have to be checked again.
- **Risk:** in my run, about 10 minutes went to starting the 4 test runners, from 06:19 to 06:29 in the log. The full run should take about that long plus a minute or two.

## Step 4: run this yourself (Git Bash, from the repo root)
```bash
TZ=UTC STRYKER_JSON=docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/146-dchan01-wm-before.json \
  node node_modules/@stryker-mutator/core/bin/stryker.js run stryker.146.config.mjs
```
- `TZ=UTC` keeps date handling the same as the rest of the suite.
- `STRYKER_JSON` writes the report to the path the course wants.
- The command runs Stryker's `bin/stryker.js` directly with your Node 22.

Some messages you might see and can ignore:
- the "Browserslist… 11 months old" warning;
- the note about the "progress" reporter being downgraded.

`.stryker-tmp/` is Stryker's temporary sandbox folder. It's deleted when the run finishes, but don't commit it if it's still there.

When the run finishes, paste the summary table at the end of the output (mutation score, killed, survived, no coverage). I'll then read the JSON and list every surviving mutant for step 5.

```text
"use client";

import { ReadonlyURLSearchParams, useParams, useSearchParams } from "next/navigation";

export const useCompatSearchParams = () => {
  const _searchParams = useSearchParams() ?? new URLSearchParams();
  const params = useParams() ?? {};

  const searchParams = new URLSearchParams(_searchParams.toString());
  Object.getOwnPropertyNames(params).forEach((key) => {
    searchParams.delete(key);

    // Though useParams is supposed to return a string/string[] as the key's value but it is found to return undefined as well.
    // Maybe it happens for pages dir when using optional catch-all routes.
    const param = params[key] || "";
    const paramArr = typeof param === "string" ? param.split("/") : param;

    paramArr.forEach((p) => {
      searchParams.append(key, p);
    });
  });

  return new ReadonlyURLSearchParams(searchParams);
};
```
